## Summary

### 1. Dependency version bumps (`pom.xml`)
- `jackson.version`: `2.15.2` → `2.17.1`
- `jackson.databind.version`: `2.15.2` → `2.17.1`
- `javacrumbs.json-unit.version`: `2.38.0` → `3.2.7`

### 2. json-unit varargs API migration (13 main source files)
json-unit 3.x removed the `withOptions(Options)` overload in favor of varargs `withOptions(Option, Option...)`, and the `net.javacrumbs.jsonunit.core.internal.Options` class no longer exists (verified against the 3.2.7 jars). In the `jmap-rfc-8621-integration-tests-common` contract files (all under `src/main/scala`):
- `.withOptions(new Options(IGNORING_ARRAY_ORDER))` → `.withOptions(IGNORING_ARRAY_ORDER)`
- `.withOptions(new Options(Option.IGNORING_ARRAY_ORDER))` → `.withOptions(Option.IGNORING_ARRAY_ORDER)`
- Removed the now-unused `import ...internal.Options`

### 3. Precise date-time error handling (`MailboxEventSerializer.scala`)
Added a custom `implicit val instantReads: Reads[Instant]` to the `JsonSerialize` class. The root cause: play-json **2.9.4** (the version this project uses) catches the broad `java.time.DateTimeException` in its default Instant parser, so a parseable-but-zoneless value like `2018-12-14T09:41:51.541` was swallowed into a `JsError` and surfaced as `NoSuchElementException` on `.get()`. The new reads mirrors the stricter play-json 3.x semantics: it catches only `DateTimeParseException`/`UnsupportedTemporalTypeException` (structurally malformed input → `JsError`), while letting the plain `DateTimeException` thrown by `Instant.from` propagate.

### Verification performed
- `mvn scala:compile` on the event/json module → **BUILD SUCCESS**.
- Bytecode inspection of the recompiled `JsonSerialize.class` confirmed the derived `messageMetaDataReads` calls `invokevirtual instantReads()` (my custom implicit), not Play's `DefaultInstantReads` — while the write path correctly still uses `DefaultInstantWrites`.
- A standalone JDK test confirmed the exception typing: `2018-12-14T09:41:51.541` → `DateTimeException` (propagates); malformed strings (`2018-12-14`, `2018-12-14TZ`, `2018-12-14Z`, `""`, etc.) → `DateTimeParseException` (→ `JsError` → `NoSuchElementException`); valid ISO instants parse correctly. This matches the upstream expected behavior exactly.
